assessment: All six retained pages were read and inspected visually, including15 numbered equations, two figures with their captions/labels, three tables, the nomenclature and11 bibliography entries. Magnified table and topology crops were used. The model is not independently reproduced; cost/distance/solver inputs and several mathematical conventions are unresolved. Underlying-source verification and public supplement discovery remain open.

sections.assessment: Liu and Isafiade, Chemical Engineering Transactions120(2025),247–252, DOI10.3303/CET25120042. Motivation combines CCS network layout, time availability, stream quality and a temporary-storage/mixing hub. The abstract's3% is reduced profit loss in an illustrative economic network, not a measured carbon benefit.

Contrasts graphical/sequential pinch methods with simultaneous synthesis; reviews Ooi's time segmentation, Tan's biochar extension and Chang's heat-hub analogy. Monitoring/administration benefits and emerging-economy resilience are proposed motivations. Bibliography citations were read; underlying primary support remains unverified. Ooi2013 is retained asB3-11 but has not yet received this comprehensive audit.

Sources/sinks/hub, periods and impurities; three topology rules; objective, transport cost, restricted arcs, production/sink bounds, hub mass/composition balances and quality constraints. All Eqs1–14 inspected in the rendered pages; native text extraction alone omits several mathematical expressions.

Modified Philippine BIOCHAR network fromBelmonte2018 with bio-oil revenue and a SanAntonio hub; this is not a calibrated geological CO2 reservoir. Source-exclusion mechanism of the earlier case is omitted, so minimum productions are relaxed. Tables1–3 and precise outage rules recorded; distance matrix, prices/cost factors, solver settings, initial/terminal hub stock and storage capacity are not supplied.

Read two exact base/forced-hub profit values, grouped-bar comparison and resilience/feasibility claims. No exact outage profits, allocations, inventories, optimiser trace or uncertainty analysis is tabulated. Text'sFigure3 reference points to a comparison captionedFigure2; no third figure appears.

Authors call it aMINLP and conclude hub resilience benefits under fluctuations while recommending hub operating/mixing costs. Published equations do contain bilinear mixing but no explicit integer variable/domain is given. The claimed general decline of profit with a hub needs separation of forced-hub versus optional-hub feasible sets.

All indices, parameters and four variable classes read. Support fromUCT andNRFSouthAfrica acknowledged. Eleven reference entries read; Diamante is2014 in introduction but2013 in bibliography. No supplementary section, implementation, data-availability statement or appendix in the retained six pages.

WithTCF$/t.km andxt/y, this TC has$/y rather than$/t. Eq1 then multiplies byx again. Summation also binds indices otherwise free onTC[i,j]. May be a notation/typesetting problem; intended implementation is unverified. Do not silently substitute a corrected linear unit-cost formula.

Bilinear equation; avoids explicit division but zero stock/inflow leavesQNt indeterminate unless constrained. Duration conversion needed with rate variables. equations.printed: Profit adds biochar delivery revenue, source-specificCf times direct bio-oil delivery revenue, andQNt1 times hub bio-oil delivery revenue; subtracts application, production and transport terms as inEq1 (15).
equations.check: Read the full rendered formula. Cf_so is outside a sum includingso; hub revenue lacks explicit period/sink sums in the printed expression. An executable model needs scoped indices. Firstk reserved for bio-oil t/t; harmful impurities remaing/t and have separate limits. No assumed conversion between these species is introduced.

variables: Indices: so=carbon source; si=sink; nt=hub; i=flow origin; j=destination; p=time interval; k=species. Narrative replaces temperature stages in the Yee–Grossmann heat-exchange superstructure with time stages. Time t is mentioned but no explicit interval-length array is given; outage narrative uses10years.

Variables: x[i,j,p]=carbon flow(t/y); S[so,p]=source production(t/y); Stor[nt,p]=hub amount(t); QNt[nt,k,p]=outgoing mixed concentration(g/t for contaminants,t/t for bio-oil species). Nonnegative bounds, initial/terminal values and explicit integer-variable declarations are not printed.

Economic parameters: CI carbon income, AC application cost, PC production cost($/t); BC biochar selling price; BO bio-oil selling price; Cf source bio-oil conversion(t oil/t biochar); TCF transport coefficient($/t.km); distance(km); TC route cost whose unit conflicts betweenEqs1/2. Numerical price/cost factors, all routes, discounts and project objective units are not specified.

SL/SU lower/upper source production; D yearly sink-rate limit; L total sink capacity; Q source concentration; Q* sink limit. Body text belowEq8 swapsD/L units relative to Table3 and nomenclature. Keep intended physical roles and literal discrepancy separate.

One hub inSanAntonio, Philippines; distances reportedly fromGoogleEarth but coordinates, routes, matrix, date and assumptions are not retained. Geographic label alone is insufficient provenance for a reconstructed distance dataset.

Perfect mixing without contaminant removal; no pressure/injectivity law, CO2 phase/composition thermodynamics, capture/conditioning energy, ship logistics or lifecycle inventory. Hub physical capacity, investment/operation/mixing costs and retained-carbon horizon are absent.

Base minima6000+12000+8000=26000t/y; maxima8000+26000+13000=47000t/y. Original minima sum36000, so the case is materially modified. Source1 outage: production0 inyear3; maximum4000 inyears4–10. Sink1 outageyears1–3 and sink4 outageyears5–10. Unspecified updates to source lower bounds are not invented.

MINLP is the authors'label, but published constraints explicitly show bilinear continuous mixing and no integer-domain formulation. Solver, tolerances, global-optimality proof and infeasibility certificate are absent.

claims.claim: Hard-to-abate sectors and net-zero motivation; world emissions grow year-on-year.
claims.assessment: Historical context attributed toIEA2012 andDiamante, not verified as a current2025/2026 fact. ParisAgreement primary source is not separately cited in bibliography.

claims.claim: Graphical approaches become cumbersome; simultaneous optimisation/time availability and a hub provide flexibility, blending, reduced administration and resilience.
claims.assessment: Read every literature paragraph; roles mapped to11 citations below. Novelty/general superiority is not independently established by reading this bibliography.

claims.claim: The formulation optimises project profit with source/sink rates, capacities, time, quality, costs and three hub topologies.
claims.assessment: All15 equations read, with dimensional, concentration/load, indexing and missing-boundary questions logged. These prevent treating the printed equations as a complete executable specification.

claims.claim: Model tested on a modifiedPhilippine biochar system with bio-oil coproduct and hub atSanAntonio.
claims.assessment: Tables1–3 checked. Removing source-exclusion changes feasible set and lowering minima changes input case. Results are not calibrated geological CO2 storage capacities or unchanged reproduction ofBelmonte2018.

claims.claim: Base profit$20336817; forced hub$19009970 because of longer transport.
claims.assessment: Both exact printed values retained; difference$1326847 is6.52436% ofbase. This is a forced-routing comparison, not the abstract's3% outage benefit and not independently solved economic output.

claims.claim: Direct models fail for sink outages while hub models stay feasible via temporary storage.
claims.assessment: Bar absence and narrative distinguish infeasible fromzero profit. No storage-capacity/terminal-stock limit, outage flow schedule or infeasibility certificate supplied; temporary stock must not be counted as permanent sequestration.

claims.claim: Hub reduces loss of profit by3% and can attract investors/derisk speculative sites.
claims.assessment: No exact outage objective table or explicit3% numerator/denominator is supplied. Plot alone cannot establish this percentage precisely. Investment implication is qualitative and conditional, not empirical evidence or a GHG benefit.

claims.claim: Hub negatively impacts profit without fluctuations; improves resilience with fluctuations.
claims.assessment: Forced-hub routing can lower profit. Optional hub with identical direct arcs and no additional fixed costs cannot reduce the global optimum because direct-only solutions remain feasible. Distinguish topology restriction, feasible-set nesting and omitted costs before generalising the conclusion.

claims.claim: Further work should include hub operating costs and mixing considerations.
claims.assessment: Author-stated limitation supports retaining economic/physical incompleteness; no complete industrial-service or lifecycle conclusion follows.

issues.action: Clarify load-budget versus strict-concentration intent with primary biochar case; exclude as a verified CO2 composition constraint.

issues.finding: No hub stock ceiling, initial/terminal stock/composition, retention loss, holding cost or operating/capital cost is specified. Perfect mixing cannot remove contaminants.
issues.action: No physical hub sizing, permanent-sequestration equivalence or general resilience guarantee inferred.

issues.finding: 3% profit-loss benefit lacks exact outage values/denominator. Text refers toFigure3 but onlyFigure1/2 occur.
issues.action: Retain published percentage as an attributed claim, not independently reproduced arithmetic. Preserve caption numbering.

issues.finding: All sources have contaminant3≥2600g/t, above si1/si3 limits1250/2500. With strict delivered-concentration limits, no purification and no initially clean hub stock, these sinks accept no source mixture; si2+si4 capacity rate17943<source minima26000t/y.
issues.action: This conditional counterexample exposes the interpretation dependency; it is not proof that authors'load-budget implementation was infeasible. Resolve before translating model into geological CO2 quality constraints.

issues.finding: Costs/prices/distance matrix, integer domains, solver/version/tolerances, full output schedules, initial conditions and exact outage results absent.
issues.action: Keep original modelnot_reproduced. A reconstruction with chosen inputs is a different analyst scenario.

issues.finding: Optional direct+hub feasible set contains direct-only choices if no mandatory hub use or added costs. Its global maximum cannot be lower solely because optional arcs exist.
issues.action: Compare forced routing and optional topology separately; investigate any contrary numerical result for changed assumptions, local optima or costs.

supplements: No embedded attachments or supplement section in the retained PDF; a public code/supplement release has not been searched while external retrieval is paused. reproduction: Independent local checks cover table sums, forced-hub profit difference, a literalEq12 counterexample, and strict-mixture feasibility bounds. These are diagnostic calculations from printed inputs, not the authors'MINLP. No objective value, routing schedule, hub inventory orFigure2 outage case has been independently solved. paper1_use: Supports conditional discussion of time-dependent source/sink matching and buffers. Case units/data are biochar/bio-oil; no pressure-constrained CO2 injection,3% climate credit or finite industrial hub service is transferred. Existing Paper1 numerical models/results remain unchanged.
